post.title: Why Winning the Lottery Wouldn't Fix It #shorts
post.description: Send this to the friend who's already spent the jackpot. Milo buys a lottery ticket and spends the millions in his head: the house, the car, quitting in style. In a famous 1978 study (Journal of Personality and Social Psychology), Philip Brickman, Dan Coates and Ronnie Janoff-Bulman interviewed 22 major lottery winners and compared them with a control group of 22 people who hadn't won. The winners were not happier overall, and they rated everyday pleasures (chatting with a friend, a funny joke, breakfast, a compliment) as less enjoyable. Psychologists call it hedonic adaptation: we get used to good changes and return toward our usual level. Fair warning: it was a small study, and larger later research on Swedish lottery winners (Lindqvist, Östling & Cesarini, 2020) found big wins can raise long-term life satisfaction. Money helps; it just doesn't keep the thrill. The small stuff is where a lot of the joy lives. Comment 'got me' if you've planned your lottery speech. #psychology #shorts #happiness #hedonicadaptation #lottery
